content:
alex: heads up — seeing a spike in NCCL P2P reregistration errors on eu-central g5x pool since ~09:15 UTC. Multiple multi-GPU allreduce jobs fell back to single-GPU.
maria: any logs/stack traces?
alex: pasting a trimmed log from one worker:
```
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_reg_mr failed, errno 22
NCCL ERROR Fatal: unhandled registration error -12
[root@node] dmesg: mlx5_core 0000:02:00.0: mlx5: mr reregistration failed, pd=0x7f
```
raj: that looks like MR rereg after pod migration/EP teardown. Did autoscaler move pods around the same time?
alex: yes, noticed a few nodes drained for preemptive maintenance around 09:10 UTC. Also saw transient high rx packet drops on the vrouter.
jin: can you run these on an affected host and paste outputs?
```
ethtool -k <if>
ibv_devinfo -v
dmesg | tail -n 80 | grep -i mlx5
ip -s link show <if>
```
maria: one quick hypothesis — VXLAN offload + MTU change + RoCE encapsulation can garble packets for GPUDirect. If encaps offload flips checksums, ibverbs/firmware might reject MR rereg.
alex: ran ibv_devinfo, sample:
```
hca_id: mlx5_0
        fw_ver: 23.27.1010
        max_mr_size: 0x7fffffffffffffff
```
and ethtool -k showed tx-checksumming: on, sc-segmentation: on (VXLAN offload enabled).
raj: firmware looks recent-ish but VXLAN offload state matters. Any UDP/TCP checksum errors in ethtool -S? If vxlan is doing hw offload it can rewrite headers and break RoCE which expects certain checksums.
jin: also check if we had any MTU renegotiation on the ToR when nodes drained. MTU mismatch silently fragments RoCE and causes rereg failures.

alex: quick mitigation options:
- set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 for the affected job queue (immediate, perf cost ~20-40% but stable)
- disable VXLAN offload on the host: `ethtool -K ethX tx off rx off` (repro window suggests this helps)
- schedule graceful kernel/firmware rollout for the pool and prevent autoscaler drains during the window

maria: agreed — prioritize customer-critical jobs with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE. We'll gate the change behind a feature flag in the job controller for 1-2 days.
raj: ops note: disabling P2P will increase GPU time and potentially bump our committed spend on the Dedicated pool. Recommend limiting to the 4 highest-priority queues only.
sre-bot: :warning: automated alert: eu-central-g5x-pool high NCCL failure rate detected (09:18 UTC). Escalation policy-1 engaged.
jin: long-term fixes: isolate RDMA traffic onto a non-VXLAN path (use native L2 or SR-IOV VF passthrough), or ensure the vrouter disables offload for RDMA traffic. Also consider flow-affinity so peer caches aren't invalidated on pod migrations.

alex: action items:
1) maria -> deploy job-controller patch to set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE for priority jobs (ETA 30m)
2) raj -> run ethtool -K disable on a canary host and validate stability (ETA 45m)
3) jin -> open infra ticket to evaluate VXLAN offload rules and a plan to isolate RDMA traffic (ETA EOD)
4) ops -> avoid autoscaler drains on eu-central g5x pool until mitigations in place

maria: I'll also message customer success for any impacted enterprise tenants and ask to re-run critical evals after mitigation.
alex: thanks — pls post results here. If canary with ethtool fix looks good, we'll roll to remaining hosts tonight in maintenance window. :thumbsup!
